answer: In a survey-agent market, agents mapping a knoll, classifying umber soil, or servicing a beacon must each lock a bond of 100 scarce tokens for 30 days to receive a daily job quota. Splitting into more identities earns no free capacity: every extra quota requires another bond. An attacker seeking 1,000 quotas must immobilize 100,000 tokens, paying financing costs and losing access to that capital throughout the lockup.
